speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are having trouble conceiving and experiencing discomfort during intercourse. To help me identify the cause, have you noticed any specific pain in your lower abdomen or pelvis during these activities?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the detailed history. Given your body dysmorphic disorder and the pelvic floor tension, have you tried any specific relaxation techniques or pelvic floor physical therapy before, and did they provide any relief?

Also, to rule out structural issues, do you notice any pain or irregularities during a pelvic exam or when touching your vagina?

speaker: Patient
text: he is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to Pelvic Floor Dysfunction.
